title: “No Fear of Eight Legs” — A Comparison of the Effectiveness of a One-Day, Exposure-Based Training for Individuals with Phobic Fear of Spiders in Large-Group versus Individual Settings
summary: As part of a scientific project conducted at Ruhr University Bochum, we offer the opportunity to sustainably reduce fear of spiders. The aim of the study is to examine the effectiveness of exposure therapy— the systematic confrontation with the fear-inducing situation—in two different settings: as an individual training or as a group training involving several participants simultaneously.

interventions.name: Diagnostics using computer-based tasks to assess avoidance behavior, one-day large-group training, a planned sample of at least 91 participants, three hours of psychoeducation and exposure therapy (in vivo), followed by a second completion of the computer-based tasks.

Diagnostics using computer-based tasks to assess avoidance behavior, one-day individual training, a planned sample of at least 91 participants, three hours of psychoeducation and exposure therapy (in vivo), followed by a second completion of the computer-based tasks.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Specific Phobia, Spider Type
Exclusion criteria:
Psychiatric exclusion criteria (severe PTSD, psychotic disorder, bipolar disorder, suicidality, severe substance dependence) and somatic factors (stroke or myocardial infarction within the past two years); for other pre-existing physical conditions, a medical consultation is required.
